To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the amplification refractive mutation system (ARMs PCR) is the most sensitive method for detection of BRAV600E mutation, with a detection level of 2% of the mutant allele, and that the hybridization probe based qPCR is the most reliable and cost effective method for routine screening for BRAF V600Emutation.
ARMS PCR is a rapid and sensitive method for detection of the most common mutation in BRAF gene, BRAF p. 600E, in comparison to qPCR based techniques.
ARMS PCR is a rapid, cost-effective method for the detection of BRAF p.600E mutation in cancer samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the comparison of three methods for the detection of BRAF mutation in cancer cell lines and in tissue samples.
the comparison of different methods for detection of BRA F V600E mutation, which is one of the most important genetic alterations in cancer.
development and validation of the new method of detection of BRAF mutation in cancer patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ARMS PCR method is a very useful tool for rapid and sensitive detection of the BRAF mutation, especially for the V600E mutation, in comparison to other PCR based techniques.
ARMS PCR is the method of choice in the case of rapid, cost effective and sensitive screening for BRAF V600 mutation in the V600E hotspot region.
ARMS PCR is the method of choice in screening for BRAF mutations in cancer patients, especially in the context of clinical trials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ARMS PCR has the best sensitivity and specificity of the tested methods and is therefore recommended for screening of BRAF V 600E mutation.
we developed a simple, rapid and sensitive method for detection of the most frequent BRAF mutation in melanoma, which is a very useful tool for screening patients for targeted therapies.
ARMS PCR is the most sensitive technique for detection of BRAFs p. V600 mutation, followed by qPCR with hybridizing probes and HRM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
different genetic techniques may give different results, which is important for the correct interpretation of the test results.
the choice of the method for BRAF p.V600E detection depends on the type and quality of the analyzed sample.

there are no universal methods for BRAF mutation testing and that the choice of the method should be based on the type of sample, the expected frequency of the mutation and the sensitivity of the method required.
